claims.text: Wear resistance of HEA coatings initially improves as ambient temperature increases and then degrades beyond a critical threshold.
The initial improvement in wear resistance is caused by temperature-induced activation of deformation twinning.
High-temperature degradation is caused by thermal destabilization of protective oxide layers.
High-temperature degradation also involves a transition from twinning-induced plasticity to dislocation-dominated softening.
CoCrFeMnNi or AlCrFeNiV coatings can be treated as single-phase FCC metastable solid solutions in the proposed initial state.
CoCrFeMnNi coatings have been formed on Q235 steel.
A sufficiently thick coating prevents the substrate from influencing the wear response.
The transition-metal matrix used in the proposed system has high thermal conductivity.
Deformation twinning contributes to enhanced mechanical performance in CrMnFeCoNi under cryogenic conditions.
Deformation twinning enhances strain hardening and therefore improves sliding-wear resistance.
High stacking-fault energy and metastability promote deformation twinning in the HEA.
The critical resolved shear stress for twinning decreases as temperature increases.
The critical twinning stress in CrMnFeCoNi is approximately 235 ± 10 MPa.
Oxide layers can become unstable at a critical thickness and consequently crack or fracture.
Temperatures above roughly 400–500 K thermally destabilize the protective oxide layers.
Thermal activation at elevated temperature causes deformation to become dominated by dislocation slip and reduces strain-hardening capacity.
Wear resistance peaks at approximately 300–400 K.
Wear rate rises sharply above approximately 500 K because of oxide-layer fracture and loss of twinning-induced hardening.
At 293 K, deformation in the coating is primarily governed by dislocation slip and the oxide layer is stable.
The degradation boundary lies between 450 K and 550 K and occurs when the twinning stress falls below the applied shear stress while the oxide layer exceeds its critical stable thickness.

contradictions.description: The predicted optimum at 300–400 K is attributed to activated twinning, but the boundary places the condition for twinning activation—critical twinning stress falling below applied shear stress—at 450–550 K, coincident with degradation.
